strategy_title: Autotune XBLOCK/YBLOCK to Fix Strided Store Uncoalescing
strategy_description: When a Triton pointwise kernel writes to a strided output (e.g., channel-interleaved layout with stride-3 stores), fixing YBLOCK=1 keeps the strided dimension constant within each CTA, converting scattered stores into coalesced writes along the x-dimension. Adding @triton.autotune with configs spanning XBLOCK in {64,128,256,512,1024} and YBLOCK in {1,2,4,8,16} allows the runtime to discover the optimal tile shape, reducing executed instructions by 3.2x (771K→238K) and elapsed cycles by 1.94x (9477→4880), yielding a 1.95x end-to-end speedup. Register pressure also dropped from 26 to 16 registers/thread, eliminating dynamic shared memory usage and removing a block-limit bottleneck.
applicable_when: Triton pointwise kernel has uncoalesced global stores (UncoalescedGlobalAccess rule triggered, >15% excess sectors) caused by a strided dimension in the output index (e.g., channel-last or interleaved layouts). Kernel uses fixed XBLOCK/YBLOCK without autotuning. CPIStall on L1TEX is dominant (>40% of stall cycles). Achieved occupancy is well below theoretical (e.g., <60% vs 100%).
do_not_apply_when: The strided dimension is in the x-axis (not y-axis), so YBLOCK=1 would not help coalescing. Kernel is already autotuned. Grid is large enough to saturate all SMs (waves_per_sm >> 1) and occupancy is already near theoretical. The kernel is compute-bound rather than memory-latency-bound.
framework_notes: Triton-specific: @triton.autotune decorator with key=['ynumel','xnumel'] triggers re-tuning when problem dimensions change. The grid must become a lambda META: (...) to read XBLOCK/YBLOCK from the winning config. YBLOCK=1 is the critical insight for stride-in-y store patterns: it keeps the strided index component (y0 = yindex % stride) constant=0 within each CTA, making the store address y0 + stride*x2 fully coalesced in x. Equivalent in CUDA: choose block dimensions so the strided axis maps to blockIdx rather than threadIdx.
